summary: The places above N are the induced places and their conjugates, permuted simply by the Galois group.

steps.claim: S is disjoint from its conjugate: no induced place is the conjugate of another, since N ≡ 1 mod the conductor and the Galois group acts on the places above N without fixing conjugates (smul_ne_star).
steps.lean:
use (by simpa [nonInducedPlaces, ← inducedPlace_mul] using fun τ ↦ (P.smul_ne_star
  D.N_modEq_one (D.p_mem_inducedPlace τ) (v := · / τ)))

steps.claim: The other fields: each induced place has norm N (q_eq_of_modEq_one), N is a uniformiser (v_N_eq_exp_neg_one), and every place above N is an induced place or the conjugate of one (exists_smul_eq_or_star).
steps.lean:
<;> grind [P.q_eq_of_modEq_one
  D.N_modEq_one, v_N_eq_exp_neg_one, p_mem_inducedPlace, mem_star_place, star_natCast, star_star, =_
  inducedPlace_mul, nonInducedPlaces, P.exists_smul_eq_or_star (D.p_mem_inducedPlace 1)]
